SEBoK Tradeoff Analysis and Decision Making, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 1 of 5 (SE-163). Second SE-internal distillation of Tradeoff Analysis (prior pass at SE-096 read it as Cluster F forward-pulverization at the decision-meeting temporal scale and as Cluster A MODA value-axis lattice). Target page is 404 in this attempt; the canonical surface is carried by Decision Management's trade-study section, which supplies the verbatim ten-step process and the MODA additive value model. The fifth-sweep revisit reads the article against §VII.7 with focus on the temporal-MODA stress-test (SE-150 anchor; SE-163 is the second instance). Cluster A MODA value-axis lattice surfaces as universal-sibling at the decision rung (five primary dimensions: Performance, Growth Potential, Schedule, Development & Procurement Costs, Sustainment Costs); the temporal-MODA reading (SE-150's Cluster A temporal-extension sub-form) confirms: the same N value-axes are co-present at every life-cycle stage with shifting weights. SE-163 is the second confirmed temporal-MODA instance after SE-150 (Whole-Life Value); the sub-form is now load-bearing across two independent SEBoK readings. Cluster F forward-pulverization is dominant at the decision-meeting temporal magnitude. Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding is the strongest reading: the ten-step procedure exists because decision-by-discretion exhibits rankism (advocate biases), and the procedural sequence binds the decision against that risk. Six clusters compose.

II. Source Read

Trade studies aim to "define, measure, and assess shareholder and stakeholder value to facilitate the decision maker's search for an alternative that represents the best balance of competing objectives." The ten-step process: framing and tailoring, developing objectives and measures, generating creative alternatives (morphological boxes), deterministic assessment, synthesizing results (value tables, value functions), probabilistic analysis (uncertainty, Monte Carlo), risk and sensitivity analysis, improving alternatives, communicating tradeoffs, presenting recommendations. MODA (Multiple Objective Decision Analysis) mathematically synthesizes competing priorities; the additive value model weights each measure's contribution. The "how much less would you accept to achieve how much more" framing quantifies tradeoffs across competing objectives. Five primary decision dimensions: Performance, Growth Potential, Schedule, Development & Procurement Costs, Sustainment Costs. Stakeholder value scatter plots visualize the dimensions.

III. Structural Read

Editorial-state observation. Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument pattern: the article is carried by Decision Management's trade-study section. SE-096 read this as load-bearing at the decision-meeting temporal magnitude. Internal-migration mode: the formalization lives inside Decision Management rather than in a standalone Tradeoff Analysis page.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D), MODA value-axis lattice plus temporal-MODA second instance. The five primary dimensions (Performance, Growth Potential, Schedule, Development & Procurement Costs, Sustainment Costs) are universal-sibling at the decision rung; each binds every trade study aspect-wise; the discriminator is value-axis. SE-036 (Decision Management) read MODA at the decision rung; SE-150 (Whole-Life Value) extended the reading to temporal-MODA (the same N axes longitudinally distributed across the life-cycle with shifting weights). SE-163 confirms the temporal-MODA reading from a second carrier: the five dimensions explicitly span the life-cycle (Development & Procurement Costs at early stages, Sustainment Costs at late stages, Performance and Growth Potential at every stage). The temporal-MODA sub-form (per SE-039 §VII.7 candidate "Temporal-MODA lattice") is now load-bearing at two independent SEBoK readings: SE-150 (whole-life-value carrier) and SE-163 (decision-management carrier). Promotion to formalization-ready.

Cluster F (pulverization, Doc 445), forward-pulverization at the decision-meeting temporal scale. SE-096's reading holds: trade studies pulverize the decision-meeting against a complete value-axis decomposition before the decision is taken. The ten-step procedure is the pulverization instrument. SE-163 is the canonical decision-meeting-magnitude anchor for forward-pulverization; SE-159 (CI/CD) anchors the minutes-magnitude end; SE-150 anchors the decadal end. Forward-pulverization spans four orders of temporal magnitude per §VII.7.

Cluster D (co-production at sub-rungs, Doc 573), decision-artifact co-production. The trade-study artifact is co-produced between decision-maker keeper (provides value-weight authorities) and analyst-keeper (provides MODA computation, Monte Carlo, sensitivity analysis). Neither alone produces the decision artifact. SE-036 named this; SE-163 reaffirms; the co-production reading is robust at the decision rung.

Cluster K (virtue constraints, Doc 314), V3-as-procedure-binding strongest reading at the ten-step procedure. The ten-step procedure exists because decision-by-discretion systematically exhibits rankism (the advocate ranks their preferred alternative above the value-decomposition; the senior decision-maker ranks their experience above the analytic synthesis) and complacency (uncertainty unrepresented, sensitivity unanalyzed). The procedural sequence binds the decision against these risks. SE-079 (Decision Management revisit) named this as the bias-mitigation V3 sub-mode; SE-163 reaffirms the bias-mitigation sub-mode as canonical for tradeoff analysis. Cluster K density grows.

Cluster B (multi-keeper composition, Doc 604), decision-maker plus SME composition. Trade studies compose decision-maker keeper, analyst-keeper, and subject-matter-expert keepers (the SMEs supply deterministic-assessment scoring). Three-keeper composition at the trade-study rung; complements SE-148's PM-DA-SE three-keeper at the engagement rung and SE-162's three-keeper at the interface rung. Cluster B density grows; the three-keeper-at-various-rungs population is now well-distributed across rungs.

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372). "Best balance of competing objectives" stays functional; the trade study describes a procedural method, not a metaphysical claim about value. Standard hypostatic discipline.
